# lfs_object_path { #labdata.gitutil.lfs_object_path }

```python
labdata.gitutil.lfs_object_path(repo, oid)
```

Locate the real content of a Git LFS object in a repository.

An LFS object is a file in the repository rather than a blob in it, so it is
the one thing that is looked for rather than asked of git.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**repo**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Union](`typing.Union`)\[[Location](`labdata.location.Location`), [Path](`pathlib.Path`), [str](`str`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Working tree to look in, on this machine or another.

<code>[**oid**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The sha256 object id from the pointer file.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[Location](`labdata.location.Location`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Location of the object in the repository's LFS store, or `None` when the object has not been fetched into that repository.
